question: Is the difficulty of naming smells a limit of the human nose, or of the English language?
answer: Of the language, at least in part. English speakers asked to name familiar odours often fumble and fall back on sources: it smells like lemon. Jahai foragers of the Malay Peninsula, whose language has about a dozen abstract smell words, named odours as concisely and consistently as colours, much as English uses red.
move: Before blaming the instrument, check whether the vocabulary exists.
reference: Majid & Burenhult, Odors are expressible in language, as long as you speak the right language, Cognition, 2014
